text.p: The following are the leading stories in the local press on Friday, June 6. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The High Court in Blantyre, the main industrial city, begins to hear murder cases this month, after more than one year without any trials, Judge Duncan Tambala said on Thursday.

- Malawians ought to improve productivity and work ethics to achieve socio-economic growth and competitiveness in international trade, Commerce and Industry Minister, Chakakala Chaziya said in Blantyre on Thursday.

- Police have arrested another Malawian of Asian descent in connection with the murder last week of an Asian businessman in Dedza, central Malawi, who was carrying more than one million Kwacha in cash.
- The ruling United Democratic Front (UDF) big wigs in Mangochi, southern Malawi, have risen against each other sparking a fiery war that threatens the stability of the party in the district.
- The giant government owned agricultural produce marketing corporation has fired 154 employees who are alleged to have spearheaded a short-lived strike which damaged some property.
